question: Which of these southern US cities will have Tesla Robotaxi service on December 31, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Atlanta is not even listed 'Coming soon' on Tesla's portal (only Cybercab testing sightings with a driver); launching from unlisted to live in ~6 weeks is very unlikely. Jacksonville was listed 'Coming soon' Oct 21, 2026 with San Antonio, Las Vegas, Phoenix; San Antonio launched 19 days later (but had prior validation testing), while Las Vegas/Phoenix remain unlaunched months after permits. No Jacksonville validation testing reported as of late Oct/mid-Nov. Florida law permits driverless service and Tesla runs Miami/Orlando/Tampa, and Tesla likes year-end pushes, so Jacksonville by Dec 31 is plausible but less likely than not. No human prediction market found (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi searched).
calls.dossier:
- Tesla Robotaxi posted Oct 21, 2026 that service is 'coming soon' to Jacksonville, Las Vegas, Phoenix, San Antonio; no Jacksonville launch date, service area, or fleet size (News4Jax Oct 26, 2026; ActionNewsJax).
- San Antonio, in that same batch, launched driverless service Nov 9, 2026 (teslanewswire tracker; Teslarati) — 19 days after the 'coming soon' listing.
- Fort Worth launched driverless Nov 2, 2026. Miami Jul 3, Orlando and Tampa Jul 21, 2026; Dallas/Houston Apr 18, 2026 (teslanewswire tracker).
- Las Vegas: Nevada approval Aug 20, 2026, still 'preparations underway', not launched as of mid-Nov. Phoenix: AZ permit since Nov 17, 2025, still not launched (tracker). Tesla's Jan 2026 plan was 7 new cities in H1 2026; several slipped.
- Jacksonville: no public reports of validation testing or a geofence found as of Oct 28 to mid-Nov 2026; Tesla didn't respond in Sept 2026 when asked about testing (robotaxireport).
- Atlanta: robotaxireport says Tesla 'has not announced public robotaxi service in Atlanta as of Nov 9, 2026'; not on the coming-soon list. Cybercab seen testing in Atlanta with a steering wheel and human driver (Facebook/Reddit reports). Waymo, May Mobility, and Zoox (testing) are active in Atlanta.
- Nov 14, 2026: Tesla opened Cybercab orders, deliveries from December, initially only in active Robotaxi regions; 8 cities cited as active (AFP; thelastdriverlicenseholder).
- Florida law allows driverless service; Georgia also permits AVs.
- Status quo: neither city has active service as of Nov 16, 2026.
- Resolves off tesla.com/robotaxi availability as of Dec 31, 2026; 'Coming soon' does not count; the support page or credible sources are the fallback.
- Event window: status snapshot on Dec 31, 2026; as of Nov 16, about 45 days remain.
- Searched but not found: Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold markets; any Jacksonville or Atlanta launch date; Jacksonville validation fleet sightings.
calls.reference_class: Tesla Robotaxi cities listed as 'Coming soon' / announced in 2025-26 and whether they launched within ~10 weeks of listing; unlisted cities launching within 6 weeks

calls.reasoning: Jacksonville was put on Tesla's 'coming soon' list Oct 21, 2026 together with San Antonio (launched Nov 9), Phoenix and Las Vegas (not yet launched). So 1 of 4 cities converted in about 25 days, and about 45 days remain. Tesla said on its Q3 call it would add 'some other cities' before year-end. Florida law is permissive and Tesla already runs three FL cities, but there is no Jacksonville date, area or fleet yet. Atlanta isn't even 'coming soon'; the only sign is a Cybercab test sighting in June 2026, so it would need announcement plus launch within 6 weeks. No matching human prediction market was found (an older Kalshi 'public release this year' market doesn't match).

calls.reasoning: Status quo as of Nov 9-16, 2026: Jacksonville is on Tesla's Robotaxi map as 'Coming soon' (since Oct 21) with no date, service area or fleet announced. Atlanta is not on the map at all, though a Cybercab was spotted there, apparently testing. Comparable cases: San Antonio went from staging (Sep 16) to coming soon (Oct 21) to launch (Nov 9), about 3 weeks from listing. Las Vegas was approved in Aug and Phoenix has been 'preparations underway' for months, and neither has launched. Florida law is permissive and Tesla already runs Miami, Orlando and Tampa. Tesla also tends to push launches toward year-end targets (its goal is about a dozen states by end of 2026). With about 6 weeks left, I put Jacksonville at roughly 35%. Atlanta has to go from unlisted to live in 6 weeks, so I put it at about 8%, positively correlated with Jacksonville. Market check: none found on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold.

calls.reasoning: As of mid-Nov 2026 neither city has live Tesla Robotaxi service. Jacksonville has been 'coming soon' since Oct 21 with no date, service area, fleet or validation sightings. 1 of 4 cities from that batch (San Antonio, which had staged vehicles beforehand) has launched; Las Vegas and Phoenix have been stuck for months. Florida's permissive law, Tesla's three existing FL cities and its 'some other cities before year-end' guidance keep Jacksonville plausible at ~34%. Atlanta is unlisted, with only Cybercab test sightings, so going unlisted to live in 6 weeks is ~6%, correlated with Jacksonville. No human prediction market found.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on all the facts: Jacksonville 'coming soon' since Oct 21 with no date, Atlanta unlisted, San Antonio launched 19 days after listing, Las Vegas/Phoenix stalled, no market. The spread (Jacksonville 31-45%) is pure judgment. I checked whether Jacksonville had launched or been dated since Nov 9: nothing new, still coming soon with no date. I checked for any Atlanta listing: none; robotaxireport says no service as of Oct 29, and the only activity is a Cybercab tested with a driver. With no new evidence, I take my own read. San Antonio's quick launch came after visible staging that Jacksonville lacks, and the other two cities in the batch have stalled, but Florida's regulatory ease and Tesla's year-end push are real. Jacksonville total ~34%, Atlanta ~6%, both positively correlated.
